content.text:
Confirmed both details. Here's the resulting behavior.

## The grammar becomes prefix-determined

Today the first segment is *ambiguous*: two segments meant native, three meant forge-prefixed. After integrating #2252, **the leading token alone decides which grammar is tried** — `et/` → native, `gh/` → mirror, `entire://` → passthrough, anything else → nothing. Leading slash stays optional on the two ref forms.

That's the whole conceptual shift, and it makes my item-1 dispatch exact rather than heuristic: "did the ref declare this parser's token" *is* the parser's own first check.

## Behavior table

| input | outcome |
| --- | --- |
| `/et/paul/dogbark`, `et/paul/dogbark` | ✅ clones the native repo from its home cluster |
| `/gh/acme/app`, `gh/acme/app` | ✅ clones the mirror (cluster picker if multi-placement) |
| `entire://host/et/p/r`, `entire://host/gh/o/r` | ✅ forwarded to `git clone` verbatim |
| `/et/paul/dogbark.git`, `/gh/acme/app.git` | ✅ suffix dropped → `dogbark` / `app` |
| `/et/foo_bar/dogbark` | ❌ `project "foo_bar" must be 3-32 characters of letters, digits and '-'…` |
| `/et/paul/dog_bark` | ❌ `repo "dog_bark" must be 1-64 characters…` |
| `/et/ab/dogbark` | ❌ same project rule — **locally**, no control-plane round trip |
| `/et/paul`, `/et/`, `/et/p/r/extra` | ❌ `expected /et/<project>/<repo>…` with the segment count |
| `/gh/foo_bar/baz`, `/gh/acme` | ❌ the mirror parser's reason (unchanged) |
| **`paul/dogbark`** | ❌ **shape list** — this is the behavior change |
| `dogbark`, `/gl/foo/bar`, `//et/p/r` | ❌ shape list |
| `git@github.com:acme/app`, `https://github.com/acme/app` | ❌ but hinted: `pass GitHub mirrors as /gh/acme/app` |
| `github.com/acme/app` | ❌ shape list, **no hint** — see below |
| `entire://et/p/r` (token in the host slot) | ❌ but `git-remote-entire` gives the actionable message (my item 4) |

The shape list itself shortens to `/et/<project>/<repo>, /gh/<owner>/<repo>, or a full entire:// URL`.

The one category that *disappears* is "looks like a shorthand but has a bad name" — what `paul/.foo` used to be. Every rejected ref now either declares a token and gets a precise reason, or declares none and gets the list.

## What I'd delete as obsolete

The 3-char project minimum stops being load-bearing. Right now my code and CLAUDE.md justify it as *what makes the shorthand unambiguous* — that's why I could delete the old explicit `gh`/`et` guard, and it's what `TestForgeTokensCannotBeProjectNames` pins. With the token mandatory, none of that reasoning holds. The minimum stays (server parity, still saves a round trip on `/et/ab/x`), but I'd drop that test and rewrite the justification, plus two comments that mention the shorthand. Leaving them would assert a rationale the grammar no longer has, which is worse than saying nothing.

## One deliberate non-change

`declaresForge` becomes redundant *in principle* — the parsers now key on the same leading token. The altitude review's suggested fix (parsers return a "not my grammar" sentinel; the dispatcher shows the first real reason) would delete it. I'd still keep it, because `explain_repo.go:111` wraps `parseMirrorCloneRef`'s error with `%w` and renders it verbatim to `explain --repo` users, so turning that into a sentinel changes an unrelated command's message. Two grammars doesn't pay for that yet.

## Two things #2252 newly unlocks — your call

**(a) `github.com/acme/app` could get the `/gh/` hint.** It currently falls to the shape list, which doesn't mention GitHub at all. The blocker was that `gitHubBareRe`'s `github.com/` prefix is *optional*, so admitting it would also match a bare `foo/bar` and answer a would-be native shorthand with "pass GitHub mirrors as /gh/foo/bar" — precisely the trap #2223 closed. A new regex requiring the literal `github.com/` prefix fixes that cleanly. Small, clearly an improvement.

**(b) A bare two-segment ref could name both candidates** — `paul/dogbark` → *"did you mean `/et/paul/dogbark` or `/gh/paul/dogbark`?"* instead of the generic list. This is exactly what people typed before, so it's the input that'll sting; naming both is honest (no guessing which they meant) and actionable. I'd recommend this one, but it is a product-flavoured choice on someone else's revert, so I'm not folding it in unasked.

Want me to integrate #2252 plain, or with (a), (b), or both? Also worth deciding: keep the commit attributed to toothbrush's change in the message, and note on #2252 that it's been absorbed here so it can be closed rather than rebased.

49:- Checkpoint reads on a partial clone no longer hammer the remote one blob at a time. `entire checkpoint explain` could trigger a Git lazy fetch per missing blob per promisor remote before reaching its own batched prefetch, so blob-existence probes and fallback reads now set `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1`, and the probe settles a whole candidate set with one `git cat-file --batch-check` rather than one subprocess per blob. Two hook paths — post-commit attribution and the stop hook's turn finalize — opened the checkpoint store with a ref fetcher and no blob fetcher, so with lazy fetch off a filtered-out `metadata.json` read as "checkpoint not found": attribution was skipped, the finalized transcript never reached its checkpoints, and nothing above DEBUG said why. Both now carry a blob fetcher bounded by a 15s whole-call budget with non-interactive SSH, memoized so a dead network costs one budget per store instead of one per checkpoint ([#2141](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2141), [#2145](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2145), [#2146](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2146))
102:- On the git-refs backend, a fresh clone discovers checkpoints without a dedicated `checkpoint_remote` — `checkpoint list` and the branch view ls-remote the read candidates and merge the listings ([#1956](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1956))
121:- `entire enable` no longer downloads the whole checkpoint archive on a fresh clone — 31s and a silent give-up on every run became 0.9s ([#1994](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1994))
122:- Checkpoint `metadata.json` could outgrow GitHub's 100MB blob limit and make `entire/checkpoints/v1` permanently unpushable. Nested git checkouts under the repo root (agent worktrees, vendored clones) are excluded from worktree status the way git itself excludes them, and `files_touched` is deduped at the checkpoint write boundary ([#1937](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1937), [#1969](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1969))
138:- Go bumped to 1.26.6, clearing six stdlib advisories, plus go-git (for partial-clone promisor bookkeeping), ogen, posthog-go, x/mod, lipgloss, and x/ansi bumps ([#1945](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1945), [#1971](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1971), [#1988](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1988), [#2005](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2005))

repo clone: require the forge prefix on every ref

Integrates #2252 (thanks @toothbrush) and builds two things on top of it.

The bare `<project>/<repo>` shorthand is gone; a native ref names its
`et/` token, so the leading token alone decides which grammar is tried.
`<owner>/<repo>` and `<project>/<repo>` are the same shape, so any default
would let one namespace shadow the other — register `acme/tool` in
whichever namespace the CLI prefers and a ref the user believes names the
other one silently resolves, then gets cloned and run. There is no safe
default, so there is none.

TestCloneRefAlwaysRequiresItsForgePrefix pins that at every layer rather
than just in the parser a refactor might route around: neither grammar
accepts a bare pair, the command refuses one without reaching the control
plane or `git clone`, and an ambiguous pair is never resolved to one forge.
Verified it fails on a reintroduced shorthand — and that the command-level
assertion is the one that catches it, since the bare ref then reaches the
network instead of erroring at the parse.

Two things the mandatory token unlocks:

- a bare pair now gets the forge-qualified refs it could have meant, one
  per grammar that would actually accept it, instead of the whole shape
  list. `paul/dogbark` offers both; `paul/dog_bark` and `ab/dogbark` offer
  only `/gh/`, since neither can be a native name. bareRefSuggestions
  re-runs the parsers rather than re-deriving their charsets, so a
  suggestion is never a ref that fails next.
- `github.com/acme/app` gets the `/gh/` hint it used to miss.
  parseHostedGitHubURL can now take the host-qualified bare form, because
  the shape it had to stay away from — an unqualified pair — is no longer
  a native ref. It still refuses the unqualified form: that would be the
  same namesquatting guess in a different place.

Dropped as obsolete: TestForgeTokensCannotBeProjectNames and the claim
that the 3-char project minimum is load-bearing. It was what made the
shorthand unambiguous; with the token mandatory the bounds are server
parity only, and what they still buy is a local error instead of a round
trip. Merged main in for the #2185 changelog entry this amends.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF

## The security test

I framed it as the invariant rather than as parser mechanics, since that's the point:

```
TestCloneRefAlwaysRequiresItsForgePrefix
├── neither grammar accepts a bare pair
├── the command refuses before the control plane or git
└── an ambiguous pair is never resolved to one forge
```

It covers seven namesquat-shaped inputs (`entireio/cli`, `paul/dogbark`, leading/trailing slash, case variants, `.git`, `acme/tool`) plus `github.com/acme/tool` and an https URL, and asserts three layers: both parsers reject; the command fails with the *parse* error while a recording httptest server sees **zero requests** and stderr never says `Cloning`; and for a pair both grammars accept, the message names both `/et/` and `/gh/`.

**I checked it actually fails.** Reintroducing the shorthand in `parseNativeCloneRef` turns it red at both layers — and the command-level assertion is the one that matters, because the bare ref then reaches the network and returns a control-plane 500 instead of erroring at the parse. That's the leak, caught. Reverted and re-verified green.

## The rest of the integration

`et/` is now mandatory, so the leading token alone decides the grammar. Both additions you asked for are in:

- **`paul/dogbark`** → `did you mean /et/paul/dogbark or /gh/paul/dogbark?` — one candidate per grammar that would *actually* parse, so `paul/dog_bark` and `ab/dogbark` offer only `/gh/` (an underscore and a two-char project are legal on GitHub, impossible natively). `bareRefSuggestions` re-runs the parsers rather than re-deriving their charsets, so a suggestion can't be a ref that fails next — and both are always offered when both fit, since naming one is the namesquatting default in friendlier clothing.
- **`github.com/acme/app`** → `pass GitHub mirrors as /gh/acme/app`. `parseHostedGitHubURL` takes the host-qualified bare form now; it still refuses the unqualified one, for exactly the reason above.

Two things worth flagging:

**I deleted `TestForgeTokensCannotBeProjectNames`** and the claim that the 3-char project minimum is load-bearing. That minimum was what made the shorthand unambiguous; with the token mandatory it's server parity only. Leaving the comment would have asserted a rationale the grammar no longer has — worse than silence.

**I merged main in** rather than rebasing (commit `021cd7206`), because the `#2185` changelog entry I needed to amend landed after my base. Clean merge, no conflicts, and it avoids rewriting five commits that already carry checkpoint trailers.

Also: `mise run lint` briefly reported 0 issues and then 1 on an identical tree — a `revive` unused-parameter in my new test handler. Fixed, and I re-ran lint twice after `fmt` to confirm. Worth knowing that a single clean lint pass right after restoring a file isn't trustworthy.

`/simplify → 4 cleanup agents in parallel → apply the fixes`

You are improving the quality of the changed code, not hunting for bugs. Review
it for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude issues, then fix what you
find. Do not look for correctness bugs — that is what `/code-review` is for.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Review (4 cleanup agents in parallel)

Launch **4 independent review agents** via the Agent tool, all in a
single message so they run concurrently. Pass each agent the diff and one of
the four angles below. Each returns its findings with `file`, `line`, a
one-line `summary`, and the concrete cost (what is duplicated, wasted, or
harder to maintain).

### Reuse

Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change is implemented at the right depth, not as a fragile
bandaid. Special cases layered on shared infrastructure are a sign the fix
isn't deep enough — prefer generalizing the underlying mechanism over adding
special cases.

## Phase 2 — Apply the fixes

Wait for all four agents to complete, dedup findings that point at the same
line or mechanism, and fix each remaining one directly. Skip any finding whose
fix would change intended behavior, require changes well outside the reviewed
diff, or that you judge to be a false positive — note the skip rather than
arguing with it. Finish with a brief summary of what was fixed and what was
skipped (or confirm the code was already clean).

### 1. `repo_clone_test.go:186-215` — the new subtest re-implements `runCoreCmd`

`t.Run("the command refuses before the control plane or git")` hand-rolls: swap `activeCoreClient`, register the restore, `newRepoCloneCmd()`, two `bytes.Buffer`s, `SetOut`/`SetErr`/`SetArgs`, `ExecuteContext`, then read `err` + `errOut`. ```go
func runCoreCmd(t *testing.T, newCmd func() *cobra.Command, srvURL string, args ...string) (stdout, stderr string, err error)
```

`newRepoCloneCmd` matches `func() *cobra.Command` exactly, and the loop body collapses to:

_, errOut, err := runCoreCmd(t, newRepoCloneCmd, srv.URL, ref)
```

`gitHubHostedBareRe` cannot be *composed* out of `gitHubBareRe` (you can't make an optional group mandatory), so the new pattern itself is justified. But it takes `gitHubOwnerPat + "/" + gitHubRepoPat` to five verbatim copies: `repo_mirror_probe.go:40,41,42,50` and `repo_clone.go:23`. Four of those five also repeat `(?:\.git)?$`.

Concrete fix — extract the shared pair beside the two existing pattern constants at `repo_mirror_probe.go:34-37`:
```go
const gitHubOwnerRepoPat = gitHubOwnerPat + `/` + gitHubRepoPat
```
then `^https?://github\.com/` + pair + `(?:\.git)?$`, `^git@github\.com:` + pair + …, `^github\.com/` + pair + …, `^(?:github\.com/)?` + pair + …, and `^/?` + `mirrorCloneForge` + `/` + pair + `$` in `repo_clone.go:23`. String concatenation, so the compiled patterns are byte-identical — behaviour-preserving by construction.

Cost: the charset comment at `repo_mirror_probe.go:26-33` explains a security boundary (owner/repo flow unescaped into the STS audience and the clone URL). Five copies is five places to miss when that boundary moves, and the diff just demonstrated the risk in the adjacent policy: `.git` handling changed globally this PR and these four `(?:\.git)?` groups were the one spelling that did not get the new named treatment.

An alternative that makes the fourth regex earn itself outright: narrow `gitHubBareRe` to the host-less form (`^` + pair + `(?:\.git)?$`) and give `parseGitHubURL` all four regexes. Same count, but the "optional host" subtlety the new comment has to explain disappears.

`pathForges` (new) keys on `"gh"`/`"et"`; `mirrorCloneForge = "gh"` (new, `repo_clone.go:30`) and `nativeCloneForge = "et"` (`repo_clone.go:70`) spell the same two literals in `cli`. `gitremote` exports no token value — only `IsSupportedForge(string) bool` and `ForgePathLabels(string) string` — so the `cli` side cannot obtain them and no test relates the two sets.

This matters because of what the two ends do jointly: `cmd/git-remote-entire/main.go:293-300` gates on `gitremote.IsSupportedForge(seg[0])` and then prints `entire repo clone /<seg>`, i.e. `pathForges` decides which refs get *suggested* while `nativeCloneForge`/`mirrorCloneForge` decide which get *accepted*. That is exactly the invariant `pathForges`'s own doc comment invokes when it excludes `/git/` ("admitting it would have callers suggest a command that then fails") — enforced by omission for `git`, unenforced for a future rename of either token.

Cheapest fix, no import change: a guard assertion in `repo_clone_test.go` next to the existing token tests —
```go
require.True(t, gitremote.IsSupportedForge(nativeCloneForge))
require.True(t, gitremote.IsSupportedForge(mirrorCloneForge))
```
Structural fix: export `gitremote.ForgeGitHub`/`ForgeNative`, build `pathForges` from them, and define the two `cli` constants as those (no cycle — `gitremote` imports stdlib only, and `cli` already imports it from ten files including `trail_cmd.go`, which is where `nativeCloneForge` is now consumed at `trail_cmd.go:2291`).

### 4. `repo_clone.go:184` — `gitDirSuffix` lives in `cli`, but its documented owner is `gitremote`

Not re-litigating whether the constant should exist. The reuse point is placement: the constant's doc comment (`repo_clone.go:175-177`) names `gitremote.splitOwnerRepo` as the reason the policy holds CLI-wide — and that function is one of the sites still spelling the literal:

- `cmd/entire/cli/gitremote/gitremote.go:279` — `path = strings.TrimSuffix(path, ".git")` (the cited authority)
- `cmd/entire/cli/gitremote/gitremote.go:186` — same trim on the SCP branch
- `cmd/entire/cli/trail_cmd.go:2318`, `experts_cmd.go:407`, `repo_mirror.go:1321` — same repo-name trim, all literal

So the policy's authority is the one file that can't see the constant. Fix: move it to `gitremote` as `GitDirSuffix` (plus optionally `TrimGitDirSuffix(string) string`) and have `repo_clone.go:129,276`, `repo.go`'s new check, and the three `cli` sites above call it.

Explicitly do **not** fold in `gitrepo/repository.go:21` or `strategy/common.go:361` (`gitDir = ".git"`) — those are directory names, a different concept that happens to share bytes.

### 5. `repo_clone.go:116,191,206` — three spellings of "strip the optional leading slash"

`parseNativeCloneRef` (116) and `bareRefSuggestions` (206) both use `strings.TrimPrefix(strings.TrimSpace(ref), "/")`; `declaresForge` (191) uses `strings.TrimPrefix(ref, "/")`, without the `TrimSpace`. No existing helper is being re-implemented — this is duplication inside the new code — but the omission is what makes the three disagree: for `" et/paul/x"`, `parseNativeCloneRef` produces a native reason that `invalidCloneRefError`'s `declaresForge(ref, nativeCloneForge)` branch then declines to show, and the ref falls through to the generic shapes list. One private `trimRefPrefix(ref string) string` used by all three removes the class.

- **`nativeRefParses` / `mirrorRefParses` (`repo_clone.go:220-228`)** — earn their place. The `_, err := f(); return err == nil` wrapper is an established idiom in this exact package, not an invention: `ghAvailable`/`ghAuthenticated` (`setup_github.go:975,981`), `checkEntireDirExists` (`setup.go:2668`), `branchExistsLocally` (`resume_picker.go:249`), `fileExists` (`utils.go:62`), `canDelegate` (`login.go:583`), `transcriptHasSummaryContent` (`explain.go:1187`). No prior "does this ref parse" predicate exists to reuse, and the two parsers' differing arity (3 vs 4 returns) rules out one shared wrapper.
- **`declaresForge` vs `gitremote`** — no reuse available. `splitForgePrefix` (`gitremote.go:220`) is unexported, and `IsSupportedForge` is set-membership on an already-split token: it answers "is this *a* forge" but not *which*, which is what selecting between `nativeErr` and `mirrorErr` requires. Rewriting the two branches as `strings.Cut` + `switch` on the token would not touch a gitremote helper.
- **`repo create`'s `.git` check (`repo.go:135-146`) vs `nativeRepoRe` / `validateRepoName`** — correctly not unified. `validateRepoName` (`setup_github.go:1101`) is GitHub-side (100 chars, allows `_`), a different namespace. And `repo create` deliberately checks only the one rule the server does *not* enforce; reusing `nativeRepoRe` there would duplicate server-side validation the create call already performs.
- **`.git`-in-regex vs `.git`-trimmed-in-code** — do not unify these two mechanisms. Folding `(?:\.git)?` into `mirrorCloneRefRe` to match the probe regexes would regress: the lazy `gitHubRepoPat` plus an optional suffix group accepts `/gh/o/.git` as repo `".git"`, which `gitHubDotOnlyRe` does not catch. The new code-level trim plus the empty check at `repo_clone.go:276-279` is genuinely stricter than the pattern-level idiom.
- **`git-remote-entire` re-deriving "is this ref suggestible" (`main.go:293`)** vs the new `nativeRefParses`/`mirrorRefParses` — real overlap (its `len(seg)==3 && non-empty && IsSupportedForge` is a laxer version of "would `repo clone` accept this"), but not actionable: `cmd/git-remote-entire` would have to import the whole `cmd/entire/cli` package to reach them.
- **`execRepoCreateNamed` (`repo_test.go:325`)** — reuse-positive; it parameterises the existing `execRepoCreate` rather than copying it.</result>

The spellings also live at `repo_clone.go:30`, `:70`, inline at `:65` (deliberate, documented), `repo_mirror_use.go:350`, `gitremote.go:47`, and are compared literally in `experts_cmd.go:401`, `explain_repo.go:141`, `repo_mirror.go:1312`, `trail_resume_cmd.go:285`, `api_cmd.go:245`, `entireapi_client.go:59`. Not all duplicates — `mirrorUseForge` is a capability claim, `mirrorCloneForge` a syntax claim — but CLAUDE.md is what future agents read as ground truth, and a refactor on that premise would be wrong in about nine places. Either soften to "the one place that knows the set", or export the two tokens from gitremote and alias them (honest price: `repo_clone.go` gains a gitremote import it currently lacks).

## Q2 — client-side validation of server rules: right idea, asymmetric placement

The pattern is established here (several files already say "mirrors entire-api's X") and the comment is unusually honest that the bounds are "server parity and nothing more". The thing to name is that the drift is one-directional. Server tightens: CLI merely laxer, one wasted round trip, harmless. Server loosens — 2-char projects, underscores, longer names, all plausible product asks — the CLI hard-refuses a ref that resolves, the error confidently asserts a rule the server no longer makes (`project %q must be 3-32 characters…`), the only workaround is a ULID or a full `entire://` URL, and nothing detects it.

The charset half earns its keep: it is what tells a native ref from `git@github.com:foo/bar`, and it narrows `bareRefSuggestions` (`ab/dogbark` correctly suggests only `/gh/`). The bounds and edge rules buy only the saved round trip, by the comment's own admission.

Placement is inverted. The strict rules live on the *read* path, where being wrong costs a clone the user cannot perform; they are absent from the *write* paths, where a client check would save a real 422 and being wrong costs nothing — I verified `project create` (`cmd/entire/cli/project.go:34-56`) does no name validation at all, and `repo create` now validates only `.git`. Cheapest improvement without changing depth: phrase the bounds failure as a statement about the server rather than a rule of its own, so it degrades into merely unhelpful instead of false. One string, follow-up.

## Q3 drift containment (beyond F1)

The `et` refusal's depth is right — the alternative is a 404 the CLI would have to explain wrongly. But it fails *stuck*: after entire-api gains native resolution it keeps refusing, silently, with no test that would fail. It is also the second place encoding "entire-api does not do native repos" — `forgeToMirrorProvider` (`cmd/entire/cli/entireapi_client.go:54-63`) is the first, and it fails soft. Cheap containment: cross-reference the two sites so removal is one grep, and word the message as a claim about this CLI rather than about the product.

## Checked and sound — not findings

I probed the "the two agree by construction" claim on `declaresForge`: the parser trims whitespace and `declaresForge` does not, so they disagree on `" et/…"` and on bare `"et"`. But `repo_clone.go:313` already trims once up front, making the whitespace case unreachable in production, and for a lone `et` the fall-through to the shapes list is arguably the better message. The comment overstates by a hair in a direction with no cost.

`parseHostedGitHubURL` gaining `gitHubHostedBareRe` has exactly one caller (`repo_clone.go:249`), and keeping the bare form in `parseGitHubURL` for its five GitHub-only callers is correctly motivated.
